answers.answer:
Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
The API reads the token from the Authorization header. It does not set or read any cookie.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.

Only an article's author, matched by username, may modify the article.
The service compares the article author's username with the current user's username. Other users get a refusal.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

Request validation failures return HTTP 422 with an errors list of the validator's error objects.
A separate handler catches validation errors and answers with the validator's own error list, not the single detail string used for other HTTP errors.
Source: app/app/api/errors/validation_error.py:17

Creating an article whose generated slug already exists is refused with HTTP 400.
The create route builds the slug from the title and checks whether an article with that slug exists. If it does, the route raises a 400 error and does not add a numeric suffix.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65

Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
The API issues a single access token that is valid for one week and has no refresh endpoint. A client that needs a new token logs in again.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.

Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.
Deleting an article or a comment runs a SQL DELETE. No deleted_at column exists.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Legal review LR-77 requires that content its author deleted is gone from live storage within 24 hours. A deleted_at column was rejected because the rows would stay in the table. Invented for this demo.

Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
The API has no password reset flow yet. This fixes the rule for when it is built: a reset link works once and expires 30 minutes after it is sent.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Support tickets showed that users open a reset mail within 10 minutes. A link that lives 30 minutes covers slow mail delivery without leaving a long-lived link in an inbox. Invented for this demo.

The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.
Password hashing stays on passlib with bcrypt. The fancyhash package was evaluated and rejected.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: The licence of fancyhash has a network-use clause that is not compatible with distributing the API. Passlib with bcrypt was kept. Invented for this demo.

Tags are stored as unique text rows in a tags table and linked to articles through an articles_to_tags join table.
When an article is created with tags, inside one transaction the repository first creates any tags that do not exist, then links them via add-tags-to-article into articles_to_tags. The tags table uses the tag text as its primary key and articles_to_tags has a composite primary key on (article_id, tag).

Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.
Adding a favorite writes a database row and nothing else. No message is sent to the author.
Invented for this demo.
Reason: Product decision PD-8 puts all notifications out of scope until the 2027 roadmap. Invented for this demo.

Tokens are JWTs signed and verified with HS256. The secret comes from the application settings.

The register route checks the username first and the email second. Each taken value raises a 400 error with its own message from the strings module.

The CORS middleware reads allowed_hosts from the settings. The default list holds a single wildcard entry.

Access tokens are HS256 JWTs that expire one week after issue.
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is set to 60 * 24 * 7 minutes. create_access_token_for_user passes it as a timedelta, and create_jwt_token adds an exp claim of utcnow plus that delta with subject "access", signed with HS256.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through passlib CryptContext, with a per-user bcrypt salt prepended to the password.
security.py builds a passlib CryptContext with schemes ["bcrypt"] and deprecated="auto". UserInDB.change_password generates a salt with bcrypt.gensalt and stores get_password_hash(salt + password); check_password verifies salt + password against the stored hash (app/app/models/domain/users.py:20).
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

Article lists page with limit and offset query parameters, defaulting to limit 20 and offset 0.
DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET is 0. The articles filter dependency and the feed route take limit as Query(default, ge=1) and offset as Query(default, ge=0), and the feed SQL applies LIMIT :limit OFFSET :offset.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:8

Only the comment's author, matched by username, may delete a comment.
check_user_can_modify_comment returns true only when comment.author.username equals the current user's username. The delete route depends on check_comment_modification_permissions, which raises 403 when this check fails (app/app/api/dependencies/comments.py:43).
Source: app/app/services/comments.py:6

Favoriting inserts a (user_id, article_id) row into a favorites join table and ignores duplicates.
The add-article-to-favorites SQL inserts user and article ids resolved from username and slug, with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; unfavoriting deletes the row. The favorites table has a composite primary key on (user_id, article_id), and favorites_count and favorited are computed per read by counting rows.
Source: app/app/db/queries/sql/articles.sql:2

Settings are pydantic BaseSettings classes chosen by the APP_ENV value and cached with lru_cache.
get_app_settings reads app_env from BaseAppSettings, maps it to DevAppSettings, ProdAppSettings or TestAppSettings, and returns an instance; the function is wrapped in functools.lru_cache. BaseAppSettings defaults app_env to prod and reads a .env file.
Source: app/app/core/config.py:19

Tests live in a top-level tests folder split into test_api, test_db, test_schemas and test_services, with shared fixtures in conftest.py.
pytest is configured with testpaths set to tests. Route and error tests sit under tests/test_api/test_routes and tests/test_api/test_errors, and conftest.py sets APP_ENV to test and swaps the app pool for FakeAsyncPGPool.
